## Objective

Deliver dossier entries precisely and keep them in context:
- persistent `systemMessage` for knowledge that lasts;
- `ephemeralMessage` for hints at the moment of need;
- deny-once gates;
- the injection ledger, with compaction and rewind re-injection;
- the pull tools.

## Design & SPEC Sections

- **v2 Design Sections:** §8.1–8.6
  - §8.1 Delivery Channels (`systemMessage`, `ephemeralMessage`, deny-once gates)
  - §8.2 Moments (Task start, First entry, First touch, About to edit, Command error)
  - §8.3 Ranking, deduplication, and anchor checking
  - §8.4 Compaction detection & rewind re-injection (X11)
  - §8.5 MCP Server Pull Tools
  - §8.6 Delivery budgets and token enforcement
- **SPEC Sections:** §7.5 (Risky-action gates carried forward), P0
- **File & Package Paths:**
  - `internal/core/delivery/` (Ledger, delivery engine, moment triggers, compaction re-injection, exposure recording)

## Dependencies & Gate Preconditions

- **Base branch:** `PR-07-v2-storage`
- **Preconditions:**
  - PR-07-v2-storage complete (op log, rendered dossiers, rebuildable index, seeded entries, v1 pipeline removed).

## Work Order Ledger

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-ledger-engine` | `internal/core/delivery/`. **Ledger:** entry IDs, channel, step index, content hash and tags (`[repo-memory <id>]`), stored with the conversation's mark state. **Engine:** a fast anchor check (failures marked `suspect` and not pushed); ranking (exact anchor > directory; invariant > failure-signature > ruled-out > rest; verified > unverified; most evidence); budget enforcement per channel. The exposure list (entries pushed or pulled) is recorded here, so the echo filter has data from day one. | architect | ☐ Planned |
| 2 | `wo2-persistent-pushes` | `PreInvocation` as `systemMessage`, or as `userMessage` if X5 says so. **Task start** (`initialNumSteps <= 1`): relevant dossiers from prompt terms and branch diff paths, ≤ 500 tokens. **First entry** into a dossier: module-wide invariants, ≤ 150 tokens, once per dossier per conversation. **First touch** of an anchor: file- or symbol-specific entries, ≤ 150 tokens, once per anchor per conversation. Branch diff paths are precomputed in the tick, not computed in the hook. A one-line correction is posted when the agent's own edit breaks an injected entry's anchor. | architect | ☐ Planned |
| 3 | `wo3-ephemeral-and-errors` | **About-to-edit pointer**, ≤ 50 tokens. **Error matching:** on `PostToolUse` for a failed command, read the output from the transcript's `GENERIC` step at `stepIdx`. A match needs the error pattern **and** either the command prefix or an active dossier scope. Deliver the fix as `ephemeralMessage`, ≤ 200 tokens. | standard | ☐ Planned |
| 4 | `wo4-gates` | `PreToolUse` deny-once for entries marked `gate: edit` ("[REPO-MEMORY `<id>`] why / do. Re-issue the edit after checking this."), acknowledged per conversation and entry. `force_ask` for invariants that need a human. Risky-action gates (SPEC §7.5) carried forward. Follows the X9 contract. | standard | ☐ Planned |
| 5 | `wo5-compaction-reinjection` | On every `PreInvocation`, read the transcript from the last offset. Detect compaction (a `CHECKPOINT` after an injection's step) and rewind (transcript shorter, or the step's timestamp changed). Re-inject one consolidated `systemMessage` of still-relevant entries, ≤ 1k tokens; skip tags that survive in the checkpoint text. Re-arm first-entry and first-touch dedupe. **X11.** | architect | ☐ Planned |
| 6 | `wo6-pull-tools` | `internal/mcpserver/`. MCP server tools: `memory.brief` (dossier-based, resolving aliases), `memory.why` (entry with short evidence spans), `memory.history`, `memory.search` (FTS over entries), `memory.note` (to the inbox), `memory.stats`. Pulls are recorded in the exposure list. | standard | ☐ Planned |

- X5 confirmed in production code; **X11:** detection on ≥ 95% of checkpoints, with re-injected entries present afterwards.
- All moments deliver correctly, budgets are respected, ranking is correct, and suspect entries are not pushed.
- Gates deny once, then allow the retry.

# PR-09: X6-lite Early Kill Gate

> **Programme:** repo-memory
> **PR:** pr-09-v2-x6-lite
> **Base branch:** PR-08-v2-delivery
> **Status:** ☐ Planned
> **SPEC ref:** [SPEC.md](../../../SPEC.md) v0.10
> **Plan ref:** [PROGRAM-PLAN.md](../programme-repo-memory/PROGRAM-PLAN.md)

## Objective

Answer the project's central question before building distillation and consolidation: **do delivered dossiers make agents better on this repository's work?** It uses time-cut dossiers from PR-07 seeding, delivered by PR-08, under the X6 protocol.

## Design & SPEC Sections

- **v2 Design Sections:** §12 (X6 B1 Replay Evaluation), §2.3
- **v2 Decisions:** PD21 (Read side first), PD22 (Early kill gate), PD23 (X6 protocol)

### X6 Protocol (shared by X6-lite and X6, PD23)

The protocol is written down and approved by the user before any run.

1. **Work orders.**
   - 6–8 completed work orders that have executable exit tests.
   - Chosen where earlier knowledge plausibly matters: they depend on decisions, dead ends or external behaviour found in earlier work orders.
   - Include at least two where a no-memory run is expected to struggle.
2. **Time cut.** For each work order, dossiers are built only from sessions, PA reports and commits **before that work order's parent commit**. PA documents are also taken as of the parent commit. Nothing from the target work order's own sessions, or anything later, may appear in any condition.
3. **Conditions:**
   - (a) no memory;
   - (b) PA documents as of the parent commit;
   - (c) time-cut dossiers delivered through the PR-08 mechanism.
4. **Seeds.** At least 2 per work order and condition. A third is added where results disagree.
5. **Metrics:**
   - Primary: the share of exit tests passing.
   - Secondary: steps and total tokens.
   - The pass threshold is fixed in advance: (c) beats (a) on the primary metric, aggregated over work orders. "Match PA at fewer tokens" is reported, not gating, for X6-lite.
6. **Budget.** Estimate the quota per run, and schedule runs across the 5-hour and weekly pools. The user approves the budget.
7. **Snapshot.** Copy the candidate work orders' transcripts and PA files into the evidence store immediately, before pruning removes them (PD17).

## Dependencies & Gate Preconditions

- **Base branch:** `PR-08-v2-delivery`
- **Preconditions:**
  - PR-08-v2-delivery complete (delivery engine, hooks, ledger, MCP tools working against dossiers).
  - PR-07-v2-storage complete (`--before <commit>` time-cut seeding ready).
  - Candidate work order transcripts and PA files snapshotted into evidence store before pruning removes them (PD17).
- **Mandatory Gate Requirement:** The protocol, selected work orders, and quota budget **MUST be approved by the user before any run begins**.

## Work Order Ledger

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-protocol` | Write the pre-registered protocol: work-order selection with reasons, time cuts, conditions, seeds, primary and secondary metrics, threshold, and quota budget and schedule. The user approves it before any run. | interactive | ☐ Planned |
| 2 | `wo2-dossier-build` | For each selected work order, build time-cut dossiers with `--before <parent commit>`, and time-cut PA documents. The user reviews the dossiers for leakage and accuracy. | standard | ☐ Planned |
| 3 | `wo3-replay-harness` | A harness that checks out the parent commit, runs a worker on the work order's text under each condition, and collects test results, steps and tokens. Reuse the PR-03 eval harness. | standard | ☐ Planned |
| 4 | `wo4-runs` | Execute the runs to the schedule and budget. | interactive | ☐ Planned |
| 5 | `wo5-report-decision` | Report the results against the pre-registered threshold. Recommend continue, redirect (for example, delivery-only with PA-sourced dossiers) or stop. The user decides. | standard | ☐ Planned |

## Exit Criteria

- **Early kill gate:** time-cut dossiers beat no-memory on the primary metric. If not, the project stops or is redirected by user decision.
- Results, including the PA comparison and token costs, recorded in `docs/experiments/X6-lite.md`.

## Human Tasks

- **Protocol & Budget Approval:** Approve the pre-registered X6 protocol, work-order selections, and quota budget before any run (wo1).
- **Leakage Review:** Review the time-cut dossiers for leakage and accuracy (wo2).
- **Gate Decision:** Decide continue, redirect (e.g. delivery-only with PA-sourced dossiers), or stop based on the evaluation report (wo5).

## Risks

- **X6 leakage:** Dossiers contain knowledge from the target work order or later. Mitigation: Enforce strict time cut by parent commit for dossiers and PA documents; user leakage review before runs.
- **X6 too small to detect effects:** Sample noise obscures true impact. Mitigation: Pre-registered metric; 6–8 work orders chosen with headroom; ≥ 2 seeds per condition (adding a 3rd on disagreement).
- **Conversation pruning destroys inputs:** Antigravity pruning (~500 conversations kept, ~19 days) removes candidate transcripts. Mitigation: Snapshot candidate work order transcripts and PA files into the evidence store in advance (PD17 / PR-05 wo3).
- **Dossiers don't improve outcomes:** Time-cut dossiers fail to beat no-memory. Mitigation: The early kill gate stops or redirects the programme before investing in distillation (PR-10) and consolidation (PR-11).

## Objective

Produce knowledge continuously:
- turn notes at milestones;
- marks;
- the subagent registry;
- the preparation layer;
- the lean-agent fallback;
- note quality validated on real work (X2).

  - Commit (`git commit` succeeded)
  - PR opened (`gh pr create` succeeded)

  - Loop protection: as specified in v2 design

  - `internal/core/state/` (per-conversation marks, subagent registry)
  - `internal/core/pipeline/prepare/` (§5.6 defences, sanitized container records, validator)

- **Base branch:** `PR-09-v2-x6-lite`

## Exit Criteria

- Harvest succeeds on ≥ 95% of ≥ 30 milestone requests; non-milestone turns stay silent; the settings work.
- Marks are correct through rewinds and checkpoints; subagents are excluded.
- **X10:** derailed outputs ≤ 2% on the test set, none reaching the inbox.
- The fallback produces notes within the quota budget.
- **X2:** notes judged at least as useful in ≥ 50% of pairs, at ≤ ⅓ of the length.

## Human Tasks

- **Blind-Judge Note Pairs (X2):** Blind-judge the X2 note pairs comparing turn notes against matching PA completion-report sections (wo6).
- **Role Opt-Out Confirmation:** Confirm the role opt-out settings for PA and worker sessions (wo1).

## Risks

- **Turn notes disrupt PA or worker sessions:** Continuation prompts could disrupt PA orchestration or worker completion reports. Mitigation: Use X1 prototype observations; configure role opt-out for PA/workers; non-milestone turns stay silent.
- **Users find end-of-turn notes noisy:** Visible continuations or unexpected messages. Mitigation: Strict milestone gate, 30-minute cooldown, daily cap of 20 per repository, and `turn_notes: on | fallback-only | off` config.
- **Processing models follow instructions in their input:** Sidecar or turn-note models misdirected by instructions in transcripts or artifacts. Mitigation: §5.6 defences (preparation layer in wo4), strip file reads and injected prompts, delimited JSON containers, output validation, and X10 test set verification (derailed outputs ≤ 2%).
- **Agents write wrong or self-serving notes:** Erroneous claims recorded into memory. Mitigation: Citations required; `verified` status only from tests, commands, merges, or humans; downstream anchor validation and memory-PR review.
- **Quota counts cached tokens at full rate:** High cost for turn-note continuations. Mitigation: Milestone-only gate; fallback-only option; quota-guard enforcement.
